name: Citus
tagline: Postgres extension that shards tables across nodes for multi-tenant SaaS and real-time analytics.
description: Citus is an open-source PostgreSQL extension, owned by Microsoft since 2019, that turns a group of Postgres servers into one distributed database. You mark tables as distributed (sharded by a column such as tenant_id) or reference (replicated everywhere), and the coordinator rewrites and parallelizes queries across worker nodes, with co-located joins and foreign keys within a shard group. Because it is an extension rather than a fork, it tracks new Postgres majors quickly and keeps the rest of the ecosystem usable. It also ships a columnar table access method. It works best for multi-tenant SaaS and high-ingest analytics; arbitrary cross-shard OLTP is not where it shines.

pricing.notes: Free and open source; managed via Elastic Clusters in Azure Database for PostgreSQL.

managedServices.name: Elastic clusters in Azure Database for PostgreSQL

scale.notes: Hash- or schema-based sharding across workers with online shard rebalancing; HA relies on Postgres streaming replication per node.

strengths: Extension, not a fork: supports new Postgres majors quickly and keeps extensions like PostGIS and pgvector
Tenant-based sharding with co-located joins and foreign keys
Parallel distributed queries speed up real-time analytics
Columnar access method for compressed analytical tables
weaknesses: AGPL license deters some commercial embedding
Cross-shard joins on non-distribution columns can be slow or unsupported
Coordinator node can become a bottleneck without careful setup
Managed Azure Cosmos DB for PostgreSQL is being retired, leaving fewer hosted options
useCases: Multi-tenant B2B SaaS sharded by customer
Real-time analytics dashboards over event data
Time-series and IoT ingestion with rollups
Scaling an existing Postgres app without changing databases
notIdealFor: Workloads with frequent arbitrary cross-shard transactions
Small databases that fit on one Postgres server
